transcript.text: You can suck at math, but you can't suck
at money math. Here's 12 numbers every
entrepreneur needs to know. Number one,
lifetime gross profit. How much money
you make in profit from each customer
who comes into a business over the time
they stay. Number two, cost to acquire a
customer or CAC. The total cost for a
business to get one person in the door.
That's marketing, sales, commissions,
everything together one number. Number
three, LTGP to CAC ratio. Lifetime gross
profit to CAC. For every dollar you
spend, how much do you make? It's
arguably the most important metric in a
business. Number four, churn. Of the
people at the beginning of the month,
how many of them are still there 30 days
later? Number five, return on invested
capital or ROIC. How much money does it
cost us to expand the business and
continue to make money? Number six,
payback period. How quickly do you get
your money back after you acquire a
customer? Number seven, sales velocity
times lifetime gross profit. If nothing
else changes, where does this business
even out or stop growing? Number eight,
sales velocity divided by churn. So, how
many customers are we going to have to
be servicing at our hypothetical max?
